  Speaker’s Card/Request to Speak: If you would like to address the Successor Agency on a scheduled
  agenda item – including a Consent Calendar item, Business item, a Public Hearing item, or Public
  Comments – please complete the Request to Speak Form. The card is at the table at the entrance to the
  City Council Chamber. Please identify on the card your name and the item on which you would like to
  speak and return to the Agency Secretary. The Request to Speak Form assists the Chair in ensuring that
  all persons wishing to address the Successor Agency are recognized. It also ensures the accurate
  identification of meeting participants in the Successor Agency minutes. Your name will be called at the
  time the matter is heard by the Successor Agency. City policy is to limit public testimony to up to three
  minutes per speaker depending on relevant circumstances (unless the time limit is extended by the
  Chair), which includes the presentation of electronic or audio visual information. Speakers may not yield
  their time to other persons.
  Please take notice that the order of scheduled agenda items below and/or the time they are actually
  heard, considered and decided may be modified by the Chair or the Successor Agency Board during the
  course of the meeting, so please stay alert.

  ADJOURNMENT
  NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC
  LIVE BROADCASTING AND REBROADCASTING
  nd  th
  Regular Successor Agency meetings are broadcast live every 2 and 4 Tuesday of the month at 4 p.m.
  and are replayed on Tuesdays at 4 p.m. (in weeks in which there is not a live Successor Agency
  meeting), Sundays at 11 a.m., Wednesdays at 7 p.m., and Thursdays at 7 p.m. until the next City
  Successor Agency meeting. All broadcasts can be viewed on Cox Communications Local Access
  Channel 30 and U-Verse Channel 99. City Council meetings are also available via live webcast and at
  any time for replaying through the City’s ICTV webpage at cityofirvine.org/ictv. For more information,
  please contact the City Clerk’s office at (949) 724-6205.
  ADJOURNMENT
  At 11:00 p.m., the Successor Agency will determine which of the remaining agenda items can be
  considered and acted upon prior to 12:00 midnight and will continue all other items on which additional
  time is required until a future Successor Agency meeting. All meetings are scheduled to terminate at
  12:00 midnight.
  STAFF REPORTS
  As a general rule, staff reports or other written documentation have been prepared or organized with
  respect to each item of business listed on the agenda. Copies of these materials are on file with the City
  Clerk and are available for public inspection and copying once the agenda is publicly posted, (at least 72
  hours prior to a regular Successor Agency meeting). Staff reports can also be downloaded from the City’s
  website at cityofirvine.org beginning the Friday prior to the scheduled Successor Agency meeting on
  Tuesday.

  In addition, meetings can be viewed live at the time posted on the agenda and related staff reports can be
  opened and viewed simultaneously along with the streaming of the meeting. To view the meeting, go to
  cityofirvine.org/ictv.

  If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the
  staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at
  (949)724-6205.
  SUBMITTAL OF INFORMATION BY MEMBERS OF THE PUBLIC FOR
  DISSEMINATION OR PRESENTATION AT PUBLIC MEETINGS

  Media Types and Guidelines
  1. Written Materials/Handouts:

  Any member of the public who desires to submit documentation in hard copy form may do so prior to
  the meeting or at the time he/she addresses the Successor Agency. Please provide 15 copies of the
  information to be submitted and file with the City Clerk at the time of arrival to the meeting. This
  information will be disseminated to the Successor Agency Board at the time testimony is given.

  2. Large Displays/Maps/Renderings:

  Any member of the public who desires to display freestanding large displays or renderings in
  conjunction with their public testimony is asked to notify the City Clerk’s Office at (949)724-6205 no
  later than 12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting so that an easel can be made available, if
  necessary.

  3. Electronic Documents/Audio-Visuals:

  Any member of the public who desires to display information electronically in conjunction with their
  public testimony is asked to submit the information to the Public Information Office (PIO) no later than
  12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting. To facilitate your request contact the PIO Office at
  (949)724-6253 or the City Clerk’s Office at (949)724-6205.

  Information must be provided on CD, DVD, or VHS; or, emailed by 12:00 noon on the day of the
  scheduled meeting to pio@ci.irvine.ca.us. Members of the public will be asked to provide their name,
  identify the meeting and the agenda item to be addressed, and a day time phone number.

  The PIO office will notify the person submitting the information as soon as possible prior to the
  meeting if the information cannot be accessed or if the version provided is incompatible with the City’s
  system. Every effort will be made by City staff to facilitate the presentation.

  CITY SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS
  It is the intention of the City of Irvine to comply with the Americans With Disabilities Act (ADA) in all
  respects. If, as an attendee or a participant at this meeting, you will need special assistance beyond what
  is normally provided, the City of Irvine will attempt to accommodate you in every reasonable manner.

  CHALLENGING CITY DECISIONS
  The time limit within which to commence any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision
  made by the City is governed by Section 1094.6 of the Code of Civil Procedure, unless a shorter
  limitations period is specified by any other provision . Under Section 1094.6, any lawsuit or legal challenge

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Mayor Choi led the Pledge of Allegiance.

  INVOCATION

  Mayor Choi invited Associate Rabbi Leah Lewis from Irvine Congregation Shir Ha-Ma’a lot
  to provide the invocation.

  MUSICAL PRESENTATION

  Mayor Choi introduced Irvine resident Jay White, who performed the National Anthem and
  “May Each Day be a Good Day.”

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  2
 City Council Minutes  June 10, 2014

  2.  PRESENTATIONS

  2.1  Proclaim June 16-22, 2014 as "Amateur Radio Week."

  Mayor Choi introduced members of the Irvine Disaster Emergency Communications
  (IDEC) team and provided them with a proclamation recognizing June 16-22, 2014
  as “Amateur Radio Week.”

  2.2  National Assistance League’s “National School Bell” Award to Target -
  North Irvine

  On behalf of Mayor Choi, City Manager Joyce introduced Susan Mehrtens,
  Assistance League President, and other representatives from the Assistance
  League of Irvine, who presented the National School Bell Award to Target – North
  Irvine.

  CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

  There was no report.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS/COMMITTEE REPORTS/COUNCIL REPORTS

  Councilmember Shea, on behalf of the Orange County Great Park Contract Audit
  Subcommittee, announced that HSNO, the accounting firm providing a comprehensive
  review of all contracts greater than $50,000 related to Orange County Great Park, has
  found it necessary to end the services of special legal counsel Kimberly Barlow of Jones
  and Mayer, and retain the services of Irvine law firm Aleshire and Wynder. Councilmember
  Krom suggested that the matter be agendized at an upcoming meeting for full City Council
  discussion.

  Mayor Pro Tempore Lalloway expressed his appreciation to staff and volunteers for the
  success of the recent Super Pet Adoption event at the Irvine Animal Care Center on
  Sunday, June 8.

  Mayor Choi provided a brief report on his recent trip to attend the Aspen Accord Study and
  Discussion Tour, learning new ideas and experiences demonstrated throughout Spain that
  can guide, inform and improve future policies and practices related to energy efficiency in
  the City of Irvine.

  Mayor Choi also made the following announcements:

    The Chamber of Commerce Business Lunch with the Mayor will be held on
  Thursday, June 12 from 11:30 a.m. to 1 p.m. at the Irvine Hilton. For information,
  visit irvinechamber.com.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  3
 City Council Minutes  June 10, 2014

    The Irvine Police Department will host the D.A.R.E. Family Fair and Movie Night at
  Heritage Park Community Center, featuring the movie Frozen. Information can be
  found in the summer edition of Inside Irvine or by calling 949-724-7147.

    The Senior Fitness Expo will be held on Friday, June 27 from 9 a.m. to noon at the
  Rancho Senior Center. For information, visit irvineseniors.org or call 949-724-6908.

  3.8  IRVINE STATION LEASE AGREEMENTS

  ACTION:
  Authorized the City Manager to execute Lease Agreements with

  (Spectrumotion) for office space and Donut Star, Inc. for food service
  space at the Irvine Train Station.

  3.9  FISCAL YEAR 2014-15 LANDSCAPE, LIGHTING AND PARK
  MAINTENANCE ASSESSMENT

  This item was removed for separate discussion by Councilmember Shea, who
  expressed concern about the proposed increase of 1.04% based on the Consumer
  Price Index (CPI). Ken Brown, Director of Administrative Services, Valaya
  Chitchakkol, Finance Administrator, and Mark Risco, President and CEO of Willdan
  Financial Services, responded to questions.

  City Council discussion included: total overall amount of the increase; approximate
  cost per property owner; impact to the General Fund if the increase was not
  approved; whether the assessment is in perpetuity; whether a provision applies for
  a maximum assessment increase per year; potential cumulative effects of not
  increasing the assessment over time; request for a report on whether the City had
  the ability to recapture costs for prior years; Finance Commission’s
  recommendation to eliminate the proposed increase; and whether a separate
  assessment for landscape, lighting and park maintenance fees was necessary.

  ACTION:  Moved by Councilmember Shea, seconded by Mayor Pro
  Tempore Lalloway, and unanimously carried to:

  Adopt RESOLUTION NO. 14-61 - A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY
  COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF IRVINE DECLARING ITS INTENTION
  TO LEVY AND COLLECT ANNUAL ASSESSMENTS, APPROVING
  THE ENGINEER’S ANNUAL LEVY REPORT AND ORDERING THE
  LEVY AND COLLECTION OF ASSESSMENTS FOR THE IRVINE
  LANDSCAPE, LIGHTING AND PARK MAINTENANCE
  ASSESSMENT, FISCAL YEAR 2014-15

  As amended to eliminate the proposed increase of 1.04% based on
  the Consumer Price Index (CPI).

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  8

  were part of a separate line item or included in the line item for general legal
  services.

  City Council discussion included: total budget and expenditures thus far for
  both general legal services and legal services specific to the Second ALA;
  whether additional legal funding specific to the Second ALA was necessary
  for next fiscal year; the complexity of the negotiations process with respect to
  the Second ALA and the necessity of additional legal resources; and
  potential future liability/risk.

  ACTION:  Moved by Mayor Pro Tempore Lalloway, seconded by

  to increase the legal services budget in the Orange County Great

  4.1  COMMUNITY SERVICES DEPARTMENT FISCAL YEAR 2014-15
  PROPOSED FEE CHANGES

  Mike Cribbin, Senior Management Analyst, provided the staff report and
  responded to questions. Corinne Schneider-Jones, Community Services
  Manager, also responded to questions.

  Mayor Choi opened the public hearing at 6:09 p.m. There were no public
  comments.

  City Council discussion included: projected revenue based on proposed fee
  changes; whether any existing programs would be reduced or eliminated;
  modifying the scholarship policy to include participants of all ages; income
  restrictions for scholarship opportunities; whether other financial
  opportunities were available in addition to scholarships; impact to next fiscal
  year budget if fees remained unchanged; methodology for increasing fees;
  overall cost recovery; and facility reservation fees and criteria for waiving
  such fees.

  ACTION:  Moved by Councilmember Shea, seconded by Mayor Pro
  Tempore Lalloway, and unanimously carried to:

  1)  Review and comment on Community Services Department
  Fiscal Year 2014-15 Proposed New or Increased Fees and
  Service Charges.
  2)  Adopt RESOLUTION NO.14-62 - A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF IRVINE SETTING FEES
  FOR VARIOUS COMMUNITY SERVICES DEPARTMENT
  ACTIVITIES FOR FISCAL YEAR 2014-15
  3)  Increase the Scholarship Fund in the amount of $50,000 that
  will be earmarked for participants all ages based on economic
  income guidelines.

  ACTION:  By consensus, Mayor Choi closed the public hearing at
  6:41 p.m.

  5.1  CITY OF IRVINE FISCAL YEAR 2014-15 BUDGET

  City Manager Joyce provided the staff report and responded to questions.
  Ken Brown, Director of Administrative Services, and Donna Mullally,
  Manager of Budget and Business Planning, also responded to questions.

  Jennifer Miramontes and Debra Lee, representing Legal Aid Society of
  Orange County, spoke in support of the proposed budget and thanked the
  City Council for its continued financial support.

  Don Purdue, Senior Citizens Councilmember, asked that the City Council
  include funding for the remodeling of the Lakeview Senior Center Rose
  Garden and Event Plaza; and include immediate long-term incremental
  allocations for the programming and design phases for such an expansion.

  Russell Stein, Finance Commissioner, expressed concern about the
  reduction of funding for Irvine schools reflected in the Strategic Business
  Plan and the five-year General Fund outlook beginning with Fiscal Year
  2015-16, and urged the City Council to consider long-term financial support
  for Irvine schools. He also suggested a long-term study for future
  infrastructure and rehabilitation; and expressed concern about staffing and
  programming expenditures in the proposed Community Services budget
  associated with the Orange County Great Park. Last, he suggested the
  development of a plan to increase reserves to 20%.

  Allan Bartlett, Finance Commissioner, spoke in support of a Five-Year
  Strategic Business Plan and a Reserve Study, and urged the City Council to
  earmark any anticipated settlement agreement monies with the Orange
  County Fire Authority and the State of California.

  City Council discussion included: the City’s Strategic Business Plan;
  expiration of Measure BB; sales tax forecasts and growth rates; further
  acceleration of payments toward unfunded pension liability versus increasing
  reserves for a higher return based on interest savings; increasing reserves to
  20%; public safety personnel and training; traffic circulation and
  technological innovation; whether financial consideration for rehabilitation
  older community centers was incorporated into the proposed budget;
  prioritizing rehabilitation of Lakeview Senior Center/Irvine Adult Day Health
  Care Center and Turtle Rock Community Center based on Planning
  Commission recommendations; addressing Mr. Purdue’s concerns regarding
  funding for the remodeling of the Lakeview Senior Center Rose Garden and
  Event Plaza and including long-term incremental allocations for the
  programming and design phases for such expansion; carryover funds;

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  11

  financial commitments to the Irvine Barclay Theatre and Legal Aid Society;
  anticipated settlement with the Orange County Fire Authority and potential
  use of those funds for remodeling and rehabilitation of older community
  centers, including Lakeview Senior Center; recent and future rehabilitation of
  Rancho Senior Center; returning to the City Council in the fall with a list of
  community centers in need of rehabilitation; funding for a school safety traffic
  study and/or working in collaboration with the school districts for a similar
  study; options for using surplus funds and the potential for increasing
  reserves beyond 20%; and savings associated with energy efficiency.

  ACTION:  Moved by Councilmember Shea, seconded by Mayor Choi,

  BUDGET AND FINANCIAL POLICIES FOR THE CITY OF

  5.3  CONSIDERATION OF MAYOR PRO TEM LALLOWAY'S REQUEST FOR
  A MILITARY BANNER PROGRAM

  This item was agendized at the request of Mayor Pro Tempore Lalloway,
  who asked that the City Council consider the establishment of a Military
  Banner Program.

  Kevin Trussell, Community Services Commissioner, spoke in support of the
  proposed program.

  City Council discussion included: current banner program and the allowable
  banner types; and locations of proposed banners.

  ACTION:  Moved by Mayor Pro Tempore Lalloway, seconded by
  Councilmember Shea, and unanimously carried to:

  1)  Approve a budget adjustment in the amount of $3,000 to the
  existing banner program budget.

  2)  Direct the City Manager to:

  a) Review similar programs in neighboring cities;
  b) Identify locations for year-round display;
  c) Evaluate costs associated for a Military Banner
  Program;
  d) Incorporate the Military Banner Program into the City’s
  existing banner program in order to reduce costs;

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  17
 City Council Minutes  June 10. 2014

  e)  Identify outside sponsorships to underwrite program
  costs; and
  f)  Coordinate a ceremony, if not included in the Veterans
  Day celebration.

  3)  Direct staff to return to the City Council within 60 days with a
  report on various options for a Military Banner Program based
  on the information requested in Action Item No. 2.
